meta.title: AirDrop for Android — Send Files Between iPhone & Android | BIShare
meta.description: AirDrop doesn’t work with Android. BIShare is the cross-platform alternative: send files between iPhone and Android — plus Windows, Mac, and Linux — instantly over Wi-Fi, or a link the recipient opens in any browser. Free, no account.

hero.title: AirDrop for Android
hero.body: AirDrop is brilliant — until you need to send a file to a friend’s Android or your Windows PC. Then it’s useless. BIShare is the cross-platform alternative: send files between iPhone and Android — plus Windows, Mac, and Linux — instantly over your local Wi-Fi, or with a link the recipient opens in any browser. No app needed on their end.

why.title: Why AirDrop can’t reach Android
why.body: AirDrop is built on Apple-only protocols, so it only works between Apple devices. Google’s Quick Share covers Android and Windows but skips the iPhone. That leaves the most common real-world case — moving a photo or video between an iPhone and an Android phone — with no good built-in option. BIShare exists to close exactly that gap.

0.b: Files go directly, device to device, end-to-end encrypted — nothing touches a server. Fast, and it even works over a phone hotspot with no internet.

1.b: You get a link, a QR code, and a 6-character code. The other person opens the link in any browser and downloads — no app, no sign-up on their end. The link auto-expires in 24 hours.

2.b: iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux — one app, every direction. Send to literally anyone.

comparison.title: AirDrop vs Quick Share vs BIShare

0.q: Can you AirDrop from iPhone to Android?
0.a: Not with AirDrop itself — AirDrop is Apple-only and can’t send to Android. BIShare does the same thing across both: on the same Wi-Fi it sends directly, device to device; when you’re apart, it gives you a link the Android user opens in any browser to download the file.

1.q: What is the AirDrop equivalent for Android?
1.a: BIShare. It works like AirDrop but is cross-platform — iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux — so it also covers the iPhone-to-Android gap AirDrop and Google’s Quick Share both miss.

2.q: How do I send files from iPhone to Android?
2.a: Install BIShare on the iPhone (the Android side doesn’t even need the app). On the same network, pick the device and send. Not nearby? Share the link, QR, or 6-character code and the Android user downloads it in their browser.

3.q: Does the Android user need to install anything?
3.a: No. For a shared link they just open it in any browser and download — no app, no account on their end. Installing the app makes nearby transfers faster and unlocks every feature, but it’s never required to receive.

4.a: Yes — free, with no account. Nearby transfers over your own network have no size caps, and share links work for anyone.

cta.title: Send between iPhone and Android in seconds
cta.body: Free, no account. Install on any device and start sending — the other side doesn’t even need the app.
